text:
### Observed differences

- **A10 became frequent and early.** In the later window, A10 appears in about 70 in 100 traces, up from about 19 in 100, with mean occurrences per trace rising from about 0.2 to about 0.8; its median relative position within the trace moved from about 0.34 to about 0.15, with a much narrower spread. [OCC003, POS001]
- **A10 now sits between A14 and A15.** Before, A14 passed to A15 in about 86 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions (to A10 in about 1 in 100), and A10's outgoing transitions were spread over many activities (A46 and A16 about 20 in 100 each, A48 about 17, A15 only about 5). In the later window, A14 passes to A10 in about 66 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (A15 about 33), and about 85 in 100 of A10's outgoing transitions go to A15; consecutive-pair evidence agrees: A14 is immediately followed by A10 in about 98 in 100 of 133 observed pairs (11 traces before), and A10 is immediately followed by A15 in about half of 134 pairs (3 before). [DIR002, DIR003, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]
- **A10 and the downstream activities changed from alternatives to running together, with A10 first.** Before, A10 shared traces with A20, A22, A23, A24, A25, A26, A31, A32, A47 or A48 in only about 19 in 100 cases (in about 81 of 100 only the partner ran), and the order within those rare shared cases was mixed; in the later window, co-occurrence is about 70 in 100 and A10 runs first in about 60 in 100. The same holds for A45 and A46 (co-occurrence about 16 to 48 in 100, A10 first in about 32 in 100). In both windows A10 never ran without A20. [REL003, REL004, REL006, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014]
- **The A20–A26 group lost its fixed internal chain.** Before, A20 passed to A23 in about 99 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, A23 to A24 in about 99, A24 to A26 in about 100, and A25 passed to A32 in about 88 in 100; in the later window these successions loosened (A20 to A23 about 67 plus A24/A25/A26 about 11 each; A23 to A32 about 47; A24 back to A22 about 23; A25 to A32 only about 41). [DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008]
- **Ordering within that group reversed or became mixed.** A20 preceded A24 in about 99 in 100 shared cases before; now A24 precedes A20 in about 74 in 100. A23 before A24 (about 98 in 100) became A24 before A23 (about 85 in 100). A20/A26 and A23/A25 now appear in both orders in near-equal shares, and A26 precedes A23 in about 67 in 100 (previously essentially never). Step distances between these activities spread from single fixed lags to lags 1–5, and A20/A22/A23 now sit slightly later in the trace while A24–A26 sit slightly earlier. [REL015, REL017, REL020, REL021, REL022, LAG004, LAG010, LAG016, LAG017, LAG025, POS003, POS005, POS006, POS008]
- **A08 and A04 became rare.** A08 appears in about 4 in 100 later traces (was about 20) and A04 in about 11 in 100 (was about 21); A08's outgoing profile also changed, but that rests on only 8 later traces. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001]
- **Smaller shifts.** A15's median position moved slightly later (about 0.16 to 0.18), A45's outgoing transitions to A46 became near-exclusive (about 78 to 98 in 100), and A47's to A48 rose from about 86 to 98 in 100. [POS002, DIR011, DIR012, LAG032]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, A10 took a new, near-standard place early in the flow with A14 and A15 as its neighbours: A10 runs in about 70 in 100 cases (previously about 19 in 100), sits early in the trace (median relative position about 0.15 versus about 0.34), A14 passes to it in about two thirds of its observed outgoing transitions (previously about 1 in 100, when A15 received about 86 in 100), and A10 passes to A15 in about 85 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (previously about 5 in 100). [OCC003, POS001, DIR002, DIR003, LAG001, LAG002]

A10's relation to the downstream activities (A20, A22, A23, A24, A25, A26, A31, A32, A45, A46, A47, A48) also changed directly: from usually not sharing cases to usually sharing them and running before them (co-occurrence about 19 to 70 in 100; A10 first in about 60 in 100). [REL003, REL006, REL009, REL011, REL013, REL014]

This is unlikely to be sampling noise: 77 control-flow items qualified against about 1 expected without change, and the placement change is shown directly by successor, adjacency, co-occurrence and position evidence that all points the same way, with each difference larger than in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits. [DIR002, DIR003, LAG001, LAG002, OCC003, POS001, REL003]

The evidence cannot rule out that the later window reflects a different mix of existing variants (for example more cases following a variant that contains A10 early) rather than a single modified flow; the windows are finite samples, and positions are event positions rather than clock times. [OCC003, POS001]

Other differences:
- The A20–A26 group's internal order changed from a fixed chain to mixed or reversed orders (A24 before A20 in about 74 in 100 shared cases, A24 before A23 in about 85 in 100, A20/A26 and A23/A25 in both orders, A26 before A23 in about 67 in 100), with successor profiles spreading and step distances spreading over lags 1–5; this is a change in ordering constraints rather than an exchange of positions. [REL015, REL017, REL020, REL021, REL022, DIR004, DIR006, DIR007, LAG004, LAG010, LAG016, LAG025]
- A08 (about 20 to 4 in 100 traces) and A04 (about 21 to 11 in 100) became rarer; A08's outgoing profile also changed, but that rests on only 8 later traces. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001]
- A45's outgoing transitions to A46 became near-exclusive (about 78 to 98 in 100) and A47's to A48 rose from about 86 to 98 in 100. [DIR011, DIR012, LAG032]
